question: Al- Biruni, the Persian scholar, accompanied which invader to Afghanistan and India? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (18/01/2021) Shift 1)
options: Alexander
Allaudin Khilji
Mahmud Ghazni
Muhammad Ghori
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Mahmud Ghazni

Explanation:
Al-Biruni was a renowned Persian scholar, mathematician, and historian. He accompanied Mahmud Ghazni to Afghanistan and India. Mahmud Ghazni led 17 invasions into India, and Al-Biruni studied Indian culture, religion, science, and philosophy in depth. His famous work "Tarikh-ul-Hind" (History of India) is a valuable source of Indian life and knowledge. Al-Biruni learned Sanskrit and translated many Indian texts into Arabic.

☛ Famous work of Al-Biruni → Tarikh-ul-Hind
☛ Number of invasions by Mahmud Ghazni on India → 17
☛ Al-Biruni served under which sultan → Mahmud Ghazni
☛ Language learned by Al-Biruni → Sanskrit
☛ Tomb of Mahmud Ghazni is located in → Ghazni, Afghanistan
question_hi: अल-बरूनी, फारसी विद्वान, किस आक्रमणकारी के साथ अफगानिस्तान और भारत आया था? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (18/01/2021) Shift 1)

महमूद गजनी
मुहम्मद गौरी
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है महमूद गजनी

Explanation:
अल-बरूनी एक प्रसिद्ध फारसी विद्वान, गणितज्ञ और इतिहासकार थे। वह महमूद गजनी के साथ अफगानिस्तान और भारत आए थे। महमूद गजनी ने भारत पर 17 आक्रमण किए और अल-बरूनी ने भारतीय संस्कृति, धर्म, विज्ञान और दर्शन का गहन अध्ययन किया। उनकी प्रसिद्ध कृति "तारीख-उल-हिंद" (भारत का इतिहास) भारतीय जीवन और ज्ञान का एक मूल्यवान स्रोत है। अल-बरूनी ने संस्कृत सीखी और कई भारतीय ग्रंथों का अरबी में अनुवाद किया।

question: The Red Fort of Agra was founded by which Mughal Emperor? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (18/01/2021) Shift 1)
options: Jahangir
Bahadurshah Zafar
Shahjahan
Akbar
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Akbar

Explanation:
The Red Fort of Agra was founded by the Mughal Emperor Akbar in 1565. Located on the banks of the Yamuna River, this fort is built primarily with red sandstone. Akbar constructed it to serve as the main residence and defensive structure for his capital, Agra. Later, Emperor Shahjahan added several marble palaces inside the fort. The architecture of the fort reflects a blend of Mughal and Hindu styles. In 1983, the Agra Fort was designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

☛ When was the construction of Agra Fort started? → 1565
☛ Which Mughal emperor added marble palaces to the Agra Fort? → Shahjahan
☛ In which year did Agra Fort become a UNESCO World Heritage Site? → 1983
☛ Which architectural styles are blended in the Agra Fort? → Mughal and Hindu

question: Who among the following ended the Kakatiya dynasty rule? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (19/01/2021) Shift 1)
options: Delhi Sultanate
Guptas
Chalukyas
Cholas
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Delhi Sultanate

Explanation:
The Kakatiya dynasty ruled in southern India from the 12th to the 14th century with its capital at Warangal. The last ruler was Prataparudra II. The Delhi Sultanate under Alauddin Khilji attacked Kakatiya territories in 1303 and 1310. Later, Muhammad bin Tughlaq launched a decisive invasion in 1323 AD, which ended the Kakatiya dynasty. Thus, the Delhi Sultanate was responsible for ending Kakatiya rule.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Capital of Kakatiya dynasty → Warangal
☛ Last ruler of Kakatiya dynasty → Prataparudra II
☛ Delhi Sultan who ended Kakatiya dynasty → Muhammad bin Tughlaq (1323 AD)
☛ Founder of Kakatiya dynasty → Prola Raja (father of Ganapati Deva) around 1083 AD
☛ Major ruler of Kakatiya dynasty → Ganapati Deva (1199-1262 AD)
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से किसने काकतीय राजवंश के शासन को समाप्त किया? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (19/01/2021) Shift 1)

गुप्त
चालुक्य
चोल

Explanation:
काकतीय राजवंश का शासन दक्षिण भारत में 12वीं से 14वीं शताब्दी तक रहा। इसकी राजधानी वारंगल थी। अंतिम शासक प्रतापरुद्र द्वितीय थे। दिल्ली सल्तनत के सुल्तान अलाउद्दीन खिलजी ने 1303 और 1310 में काकतीय क्षेत्रों पर आक्रमण किया। बाद में, मुहम्मद बिन तुगलक के शासनकाल में 1323 ई. में वारंगल पर निर्णायक आक्रमण हुआ, जिसने काकतीय राजवंश को समाप्त कर दिया। इस प्रकार, दिल्ली सल्तनत ने काकतीय शासन का अंत किया।

question: Which ruler wanted to build the Alai Minar near the Qutub Minar, but could not complete it? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (21/01/2021) Shift 1)
options: Raziya Sultana
Nasir-ud-Din Mahmud
Iltutmish
Ala-ud-Din Khilji
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Ala-ud-Din Khilji

Explanation:
Ala-ud-Din Khilji planned to build a minar twice the height of the Qutub Minar, known as the Alai Minar. It is located to the north of the Qutub Minar. However, after his death, the construction remained incomplete. The Alai Minar stands at a height of about 24.5 meters, far less than the intended height. It is made of red sandstone and is an important example of the architecture of the Delhi Sultanate. Ala-ud-Din Khilji belonged to the Khilji dynasty and is known for his empire expansion and administrative reforms.

☛ Which dynasty did Ala-ud-Din Khilji belong to? → Khilji dynasty
☛ What is the height of Alai Minar? → About 24.5 meters

question: Which mosque, believed to be the first one to be built in Delhi, is situated near Qutub Minar? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (21/01/2021) Shift 2)
options: Shahi Atala Masjid
Adina Mosque
Nakhoda Masjid
Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque

Explanation:
Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque is considered the first mosque built in Delhi. It was constructed in 1193 CE by Qutb-ud-din Aibak. The mosque is located near Qutub Minar and is an important monument of the Delhi Sultanate. Its construction used debris from 27 Hindu and Jain temples. The name 'Quwwat-ul-Islam' means 'Might of Islam'. This mosque is an early example of Islamic architecture in India.

☛ Meaning of name → Might of Islam
☛ Location → Near Qutub Minar, Delhi

question: Who established Sera-i-Adl, an exclusive market in Delhi for manufactured and exported goods to be sold at prices fixed by administration? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (21/01/2021) Shift 2)
options: Muhammad bin Tughlaq
Shershah Suri
Alauddin Khalji
Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Alauddin Khalji

Explanation:
Alauddin Khalji established Sera-i-Adl, an exclusive market in Delhi for manufactured and exported goods to be sold at prices fixed by the administration. During his reign (1296-1316 CE), Alauddin implemented a price control system regulating the prices of grain, cloth, and other commodities. Sera-i-Adl was part of this policy, where merchants sold goods at predetermined rates. The market aimed to regulate trade and ensure consumers got goods at fair prices. Other options like Muhammad bin Tughlaq, Shershah Suri, and Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah did not establish such a market system.

☛ Who established Sera-i-Adl? → Alauddin Khalji
☛ What was Alauddin Khalji's market control department called? → Diwan-i-Riyasat
☛ What was the reign period of Alauddin Khalji? → 1296-1316 CE
☛ Under which system did Alauddin fix prices? → Price control system
question_hi: प्रशासन द्वारा निर्धारित कीमतों पर बेचे जाने वाले निर्मित और निर्यातित सामानों के लिए दिल्ली में एक विशेष बाजार सेरा-ए-अदल की स्थापना किसने की? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (21/01/2021) Shift 2)

अलाउद्दीन खिलजी ने दिल्ली में सेरा-ए-अदल नामक एक विशेष बाजार स्थापित किया। यह बाजार निर्मित और निर्यातित वस्तुओं के लिए था, जो प्रशासन द्वारा निर्धारित कीमतों पर बेची जाती थीं। अलाउद्दीन खिलजी के शासनकाल (1296-1316 ई.) में उसने मूल्य नियंत्रण प्रणाली लागू की थी, जिसमें अनाज, कपड़ा और अन्य वस्तुओं की कीमतें तय की गई थीं। सेरा-ए-अदल इसी नीति का हिस्सा था, जहाँ व्यापारी निर्धारित दरों पर सामान बेचते थे। इस बाजार का उद्देश्य व्यापार को नियमित करना और उपभोक्ताओं को उचित दाम पर वस्तुएँ उपलब्ध कराना था। अन्य विकल्प जैसे मुहम्मद बिन तुगलक, शेरशाह सूरी और कुतुबुद्दीन मुबारक शाह ने ऐसी बाजार व्यवस्था नहीं बनाई थी।

question: Which community has the Adi Granth as their Holy Book? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (22/01/2021) Shift 1)
options: Buddhists
Jains
Jews
Sikhs
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Sikhs

Explanation:
Adi Granth, also known as Guru Granth Sahib, is the holy scripture of Sikhism. It was compiled by the fifth Sikh Guru, Guru Arjan Dev Ji, in 1604. The text includes hymns of Sikh Gurus, Hindu saints, and Muslim Sufis. It is considered the living Guru of the Sikhs and elaborates on core Sikh principles such as one God, equality, and service. The holy book of Buddhists is Tripitaka, of Jains is Agam, and of Jews is Tanakh.

☛ Year of compilation of Adi Granth → 1604 CE
☛ Holy book of Sikhs → Guru Granth Sahib (Adi Granth)

☛ Holy book of Buddhists → Tripitaka

question: During which period did the Sultanate ruler, Ghiyas-ud-din Balban, take over and rule the throne of Delhi? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (23/01/2021) Shift 2)

question: Who among the following built the "Adhai din ka Jhopara" at Ajmer? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (01/02/2021) Shift 2)

It is one of the oldest mosques in India and exemplifies the architecture of the Delhi Sultanate period.
